text:
Rina_support: Hey team, customer_acme opened an escalation — they see a spike of 5xx errors on streaming endpoints starting ~09:10 UTC. They say many of these are from mobile clients that close the socket early.

customer_acme: We get ~120 5xxs/min on /v1/stream generate and our frontend shows a chunked stream stopped mid-response. Backend logs show 'broken pipe' and a 502 from the gateway.

Rina_support: attaching sample request id from our logs: request_id=req_48b2c1a9, model=gpt-13b-stream, route=/v1/stream. Repro steps from the customer: open streaming request, close connection after first chunk. They claim the call is counted as 5xx in metrics.

Ben_repro: I tried to repro locally with curl: `curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-13b\"` then ctrl-c after first token. I see `write failed: Broken pipe` in our runtime logs and upstream response logged as 502.

Jorge_sre: can you paste the exact gateway log lines? which component returns 502?

Rina_support: here's an excerpt from the gateway logs (sanitized):
```
[TIMESTAMP] request_id=req_48b2c1a9 path=/v1/stream method=POST upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=1243 client_closed=1 err=\"write: broken pipe\" gateway_status=502
[TIMESTAMP] request_id=req_48b2c1a9 route=gpt-13b-stream handler=streamer duration_ms=23 error=\"client closed connection\"
```

Lina_runtime: interesting — upstream_status=200 but gateway_status=502. That suggests the runtime produced output (started streaming) but the gateway classified it as an error because write to client failed. We currently propagate that as a 5xx.

Jorge_sre: Known issue: some proxies map client disconnects to 502/504 depending on where the broken pipe happens. Nginx sometimes emits 499 when the client closes connection; our gateway does not.

Lina_runtime: We should avoid counting client-initiated disconnects as server 5xx in telemetry. Two parts: (A) metric increment logic in gateway (B) what we report to customers.

Rina_support: Customer wants two things: 1) correct metrics (don't count aborted streams as errors), 2) possible server-side config so mobile clients closing early don't blow up dashboards.

Jorge_sre: quick mitigation: treat downstream write errors where upstream already returned first chunk (upstream_bytes > 0) as non-error for 5xx metric. We can add a flag: if client_closed=1 && upstream_bytes>0 => classify as client_aborted (499-like) instead of 5xx.

Lina_runtime: Agreed. Also need to ensure we don't mask real server errors. If upstream_status >=500 or runtime error before first chunk, keep as 5xx.

Ben_repro: Repro note: to trigger the bug reliably, use a small chunked response and close socket immediately. Example with netcat: `printf \"POST /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.example\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n1\r\n{\"prompt\":\"hi\"}\r\n0\r\n\r\n\" | nc api.redwood.example 443` then kill the nc process after first chunk.

Rina_support: Thanks. Customer also sent samples showing our billing flagged these as error requests and deducted credits. They want refund for error counts.

Jorge_sre: For billing impact we need to check pipeline: billing jobs rely on final gateway_status. If we change classification, billing should not count aborted streams as billable failed requests. But careful — tokens were generated and billed. We need to reconcile: customer wants not to be charged for requests marked as errors, but tokens were produced — billing might still apply.

Lina_runtime: Implementation plan: 1) Short-term: change metrics only (don't increment 5xx counter for client_aborted scenario) and tag logs with client_abort=true. 2) Medium-term: add explicit 499 classification and expose it in dashboards. 3) Long-term: ensure billing and analytics treat 499 differently from 5xx and create a customer-facing doc about streaming abort behavior.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: patch/gateway-client-abort-classify to staging at 2026-03-15T12:30:00Z

Rina_support: I'll offer customer_acme temporary workarounds: - retry on client side if they expect more tokens, - set a short keepalive so mobile clients don't close mid-stream, - use smaller chunk windows so first chunk arrives quickly.

customer_acme: Appreciate the quick attention. We do still care about billing though — is there a path to credit the bad counts?

Jorge_sre: We'll run a backfill to reclassify recent events where upstream_bytes>0 and gateway_status in [502,504] to client_abort. That will update internal dashboards and metrics. Billing team needs to decide credits separately; I'll loop them in.

Lina_runtime: Patch pushed to staging. Key snippet (gateway):
```
if (client_closed && upstream_bytes > 0 && upstream_status < 500) {
  classification = \"client_abort\"; // do not increment server_5xx counter
} else if (upstream_status >= 500) {
  classification = \"server_error\";
}
```

Jorge_sre: Running staging load tests now. Ben, can you run your netcat/curl repro against staging and paste gateway logs?

Ben_repro: running now... got the same broken pipe log but gateway_status=499 on staging. Logs: `request_id=req_stg_11 path=/v1/stream upstream_status=200 upstream_bytes=512 client_closed=1 gateway_status=499`

Rina_support: Customer is ok to test on canary if we get results.

customer_acme: we'll validate if our dashboards look better after the change. Also please confirm whether billing will be adjusted for the last 24 hours.

Jorge_sre: I'll open a ticket with billing: TICKET-9983 to evaluate credits. Action items: Jorge -> backfill & billing ticket; Lina -> prod rollout plan & doc; Rina -> customer comms and ask for sample request ids for last 24h.

Rina_support: Closing loop for now. If anyone sees unexpected regressions in streaming, @channel ping. Thanks. :pray:
